messages:
incident-bot: P0 triggered — multiple 502/CrashLoopBackOffs observed from inference-service-canary after rollout of v5. Canary 10% -> errors spike at ~09:12 UTC. Auto-escalating to on-call.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: inference-service v5 -> 10% traffic at 09:06 UTC (strategy: gradual-swap, probe: /ready). CI artifacts: sha: f2a9d3c.

Alice W: paging in. seeing the same in Grafana, 502s and readiness failing on new pod. Repro on staging? No, staging passed.

Bob K: I pulled kube events: several pods hit `CrashLoopBackOff` with `Readiness probe failed` and then HPA scaled down replica count briefly which made latency worse for stable pods.

Carol N: Pager duty already notified: @pagerduty — Alice on-call. What customers are impacted? Dave, can you check high-priority accounts?

Dave (support): Getting reports from a small set of customers hitting inference timeouts and 5xx. Looks like some requests routed to canary nodes returning 502 quickly. Customer dashboard: https://redwood.ops/customers/alerts (redacted).

Alice W: Immediate mitigation: set feature flag `use_v5_inference` -> off (kill-switch) for web traffic to stop routing to v5. Who has access?

Bob K: I'm toggling the flag now via admin console. CLI: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://flags.redwood/set -d '{"use_v5_inference": false}'`

deploy-bot: Feature flag toggle recorded (admin-ops by bob-kim) at 09:18 UTC. Rollout traffic now 0% to v5.

Alice W: Confirming traffic dropped to 0% for v5. Errors for customers decreasing but still seeing some 502s from pods that are crashlooping and the HPA oscillation.

Carol N: HPA is behaving oddly because the crashloops cause readiness to fail so metrics see less ready pods and attempt to scale, then probe timeouts prevent new pods from stabilizing. Suggest scaling minimum replicas to keep capacity while we debug.

Bob K: Increasing deployment `minReplicas` to 3 for stable pool (non-canary) and temporarily pin stable image to v4. Command: `kubectl patch hpa inference-service --patch '{"spec": {"minReplicas": 3}}'`

Alice W: Done. Also cordoning the problematic node that has several crashlooping canary pods to stop new scheduling there: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-5-12`

Dave (support): Customers reporting improvement after flag flip and HPA tweak. Noting this on the ticket queue.

Bob K: Looking at the failing pod logs (canary):
```
I0324 09:10:45.123 1 inference_server.cpp:214] model load start
E0324 09:10:46.004 1 readiness_probe.cpp:58] readiness check: config parse error: unknown field "hot_start"
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```

Alice W: "unknown field \"hot_start\"" — that's a manifest change introduced in v5's config schema. We didn't validate schema compatibility in the rollout pipeline. That explains readiness failures -> crashloop -> HPA cascade.

Carol N: Why didn't CI catch this? Staging uses a different config generator. Action item for postmortem: add schema gate in deployment pipeline.

Bob K: For immediate fix: patch the v5 manifest in cluster to remove `hot_start` key from the mounted config map so canary pods can start, or keep v5 traffic at 0% and rollback. Which is faster?

Alice W: Rollback to v4 for all traffic and abort the canary. We need production stability ASAP. Bob — can you trigger rollback?

Bob K: Rolling back: `kubectl set image deployment/inference-service inference-server=redwood/inference:v4 --namespace=prod` and updating Deployment strategy to pause canary.

deploy-bot: Rollback job started at 09:31 UTC. Canary traffic forcibly set to 0%.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-20240324-001 — "rollout exposed invalid config key causing canary crashloops and HPA oscillation". Severity: P0.

Alice W: After rollback, monitoring — error rate to baseline in 10m. HPA stabilizing.

Dave (support): Confirmed with customer-ops: latency and 5xx back to normal for affected customers. I'll set update message for those tickets.

Eve (customer-ops): Drafted status update: "We experienced a brief degradation due to a canary rollout. We've rolled back the change and services are stable. Root cause under investigation." Will post in status.redwood.com once engineering confirm.

Carol N: Triage notes: root cause = manifest schema change (`hot_start`), didn't fail CI because different config generator path; secondary cause = canary readiness not resilient to schema parsing errors, tertiary = HPA min replicas too low causing capacity shock.

Bob K: Post-rollback, I applied a quick admission check to deny deployments with unknown top-level keys for server config: `kubectl apply -f validating-webhook-config.yaml` (temp). This will protect until we add pipeline schema checks.

Alice W: On-call handoff at 11:00 UTC to Carol. Logging follow-up actions: P0 -> triaged, rollback completed, customers notified, temporary webhook in place.

Carol N: I'll run the postmortem. Preliminary action items: (1) Add config schema validation in pipeline, (2) Add integration test that boots a canary pod with production config generator, (3) Revisit HPA minReplicas for inference pools, (4) Improve flag rollback playbook with auto-verify step.

Dave (support): I'll coordinate customer communications and add incident timeline to the ticket.

Alice W: Thanks all. Adding timeline to the incident doc and closing pager duty once all verified.

pagerduty: Incident acknowledged by Alice W at 09:40 UTC.

incident-bot: Incident INC-20240324-001 updated: status -> mitigated at 10:02 UTC, assigned -> Carol N for follow-up.

Carol N: I'll schedule a 1hr postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC and invite product + runtime + devex.

Bob K: Leaving a note in the deploy-runbook: add `config.schema.json` validation step and mandatory canary smoke test that hits `/ready` and verifies config keys.

Alice W: Closing thread for live mitigation. We'll use the incident doc for the postmortem conclusions. :white_check_mark:
